task_instance: Given a 6-sprint sprint_data.json (Falcon Squad, planned/completed points, stories, blockers, ceremonies, and 6 retrospectives), run the skill's velocity_analyzer.py to produce a Monte Carlo velocity forecast (50/70/85/95% confidence intervals) plus trend/CV, as the skill's core deliverable ('Run Python scripts to analyse sprint JSON exports... Monte Carlo sprint forecasting... Produces confidence-interval forecasts').
blocker_detail: The skill's entire value proposition is executing three Python scripts (velocity_analyzer.py, sprint_health_scorer.py, retrospective_analyzer.py) against the JSON input to produce Monte Carlo simulations, weighted health scoring, and action-item/theme analytics. This office-assistant runtime explicitly cannot run code, scripts, or shell commands of any kind. I built a realistic, schema-conformant 6-sprint sample input (sprint_data.json, matching the schema in the SKILL.md's 'Input Requirements' section: team_info, sprints with planned/completed points, stories, blockers, ceremonies, plus 6 retrospectives with action items) so the scripts would have had sufficient data (6 sprints, 6 retrospectives, meeting the stated minimums for all three tools). However, I have no access to the actual script source (only the SKILL.md was permitted to be read, not scripts/ or assets/ under the source repo) and, even if I had it, I am not permitted to execute Python. Manually hand-computing a substitute (e.g. a simple average/CV) would not be the same deliverable the skill promises (a Monte Carlo simulation with defined confidence intervals and a specific multi-dimension weighted scoring algorithm I don't have the formula for), and would misrepresent an 'achieved' outcome. This is exactly the 'missing_tool_in_runtime' case per the task rules: running any code or command is an ability the runtime does not grant, and the skill inherently needs it for its stated deliverable.
evidence: Sample input created at sprint_data.json (6 sprints with planned/completed points, per-story status, blockers with open/resolve dates, ceremony participation rates, and 6 retrospectives with prioritized/owned action items) in the work directory, satisfying the >=3 sprint / >=6 recommended sprint / >=2 sprint health / >=3 retrospective thresholds the SKILL.md itself sets as validation gates. Attempted to proceed to the 'Run velocity analysis' step of the documented Sprint Planning workflow ('python velocity_analyzer.py sprint_data.json --format text'), which requires invoking a Python interpreter — an ability explicitly excluded from this runtime ('CANNOT run code, scripts or shell commands of any kind'). No workaround (manual computation) can faithfully reproduce the script's Monte Carlo simulation or the weighted health-scoring algorithm, whose exact implementation is in scripts/ files I was not given access to read. Concluded the core deliverable is not achievable in this runtime and stopped at that point per the safety rules rather than fabricating numeric output.
